Modesty is part of faith and brings nothing but good; Imran grew angry when Bushair set books of wisdom against the Prophet's words on it.
Fatimah and Maimuna screened the Prophet while he bathed; a man must not look at another man's private parts nor a woman at a woman's, nor share one cover.
Carrying stones for the Ka'ba, the Prophet fainted on baring himself and was never seen naked again; he told Miswar not to walk naked, and sought cover when relieving himself.
Jarir asked the Prophet about a sudden glance, and he commanded him to turn his eyes away.
Umar called out to the tall Sauda when the Prophet's wives went out for their needs; revelation followed, in one report permitting them out, in another the veil verses.
No man may stay the night with a married woman but her husband or mahram, the husband's brother is like death, and none should enter an absent man's house alone.
A eunuch who visited the Prophet's household described a woman's body, so the Prophet said such men should not enter upon the women, who then veiled themselves from him.
Before Islam women circled the Ka'ba naked, asking for a cloth to cover them, and the verse 'Adorn yourself at every place of worship' was revealed.
